reason: Cached bootstrap skips dotenv; configuration is the stable application access boundary.
Retry and refresh are separate maintenance response headers.
The standard application builder passes bootstrap/providers.php into provider registration.
Provider boot is a distinct phase after eager registration, and boot supports container injection.
Scoped registration combines singleton resolution with lifecycle-specific instance flushing.
The deferred manifest maps provided abstracts to provider classes.
Terminate resolves a middleware instance separately; sharing handle state requires an appropriate lifetime or external request-local state.
Trusted-host middleware establishes allowed host patterns; URL escaping and APP_URL address different concerns.
The middleware builder stores custom aliases for the HTTP kernel/router alias table.
The kernel global pipeline precedes router dispatch; route exclusions operate later on a separate list.
Legacy instance middleware discovery resolves the controller while gathering route middleware; static HasMiddleware follows a different path.
On mutex contention, the command returns a numeric isolated option value or its configured default isolation exit code.
Laravel has a separate authenticated verification-request flow; a validation rule alone does not fulfill it. No external email or DNS service is contacted in this evidence check.
The authorization phase precedes validation completion and the action. The required debit/write atomicity belongs to the later application transaction, not this permission hook.
Form Requests expose separate rule and authorization boundaries. This is an architectural contract review, not a claim to execute a particular application policy.
Session blocking coordinates participating requests through the configured cache lock store. This contract check does not claim a multi-process concurrency benchmark.
The middleware supports targeted URI exemptions. Provider signature/replay verification is a separate application requirement and is not claimed to be exercised against a payment service.
Laravel requests a write row lock; PostgreSQL holds it until transaction end. Transaction placement and invariant reasoning are documented-contract validation, not a SQLite concurrency test.
Laravel preserves the declared composite-index columns. PostgreSQL B-tree leading equality and ordering behavior is documented, not benchmarked in SQLite; planner selection depends on statistics.
PostgreSQL documents consistent lock acquisition order as the principal defense against this wait cycle. Laravel supplies the locking query; no multi-connection PostgreSQL execution is claimed.

A local transaction can commit the domain row and outbox row atomically. Relay failure-window and consumer-idempotency claims use the cited original outbox pattern; no broker execution or exactly-once guarantee is claimed.
Worker timeout and reservation expiry are distinct operational clocks. The cited Laravel contract requires timeout to be shorter; no actual process kill or live Redis timing is performed.
The worker compares a cache restart timestamp between jobs. Graceful exit and supervisor replacement are operational deployment behavior, not a spawned-daemon test.
Worker lifetime limits are evaluated in the stop conditions. This source contract does not claim a live supervisor or measure parser memory.
The source emits the event after transport send returns a message. No external mailbox, delivery receipt or read receipt is tested or implied.
The current command repeats eligible sub-minute events through the minute boundary. The long-running timed loop is source-validated, not run as a live minute-long process.
The adapter implements append through get and put. This contract check identifies a missing concurrency guarantee; it does not claim to simulate concurrent remote writes.
The S3 adapter creates a presigned PutObject request and returns its URL plus headers. No S3 SDK request or external bucket upload is executed.
The standard fallback link is inspected. Creating symlinks is intentionally disabled in the isolated fixture runner.
RedisStore flush delegates to FLUSHDB. This is a documented/source contract; no shared Redis database is contacted or flushed.
The pool result loop preserves request keys. Network concurrency is not benchmarked; the pinned Pool::as source also stores requests under the supplied alias.
Official Vite environment contract, default prefix and a referenced value. No Vite bundler execution is claimed.
Browser Fetch documentation contract with cookie and server-policy assumptions stated. PHP cannot execute a browser credential policy; no browser network exchange is claimed.
OWASP destination and redirect contract; no live DNS, SSRF probing or complete production filter is claimed.
OWASP storage/delivery boundary applied to an explicit download-only requirement. No uploaded active document is executed.
MDN browser cookie contract. This does not claim a live browser attack simulation.
Laravel official Nginx deployment example restricts FastCGI to the front controller and returns 404 for other PHP locations. No live Nginx instance is tested.
Official deployment permission contract; no host ownership or permissions are modified.
Migration reversal is an explicit operation. The release-switch decision additionally follows the stated shared-state and data-retention constraints; no production rollback is executed.
The real production-confirmation branch explicitly accepts --force. No real deployment command is run.
Official Octane worker-reload contract. Octane server software is not installed or exercised in this isolated harness.
PostgreSQL index overhead contract plus the stated workload. No PostgreSQL benchmark or production index is executed.
Documented idempotency/failure ambiguity plus the explicit provider contract. No real payment, network request or production recovery is executed.
Composer lock/install contract and the Laravel upgrade guide. This is a validation-planning question, not a claim to have upgraded an unrelated production application.
